newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen moving sideways on campaign.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen moving sideways on campaign.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are expected to move sideways on Tuesday as the market remains worried about violence in the ongoing general election campaign despite a consensus by the three contesting parties to cease street rallies, brokers said.
The minority United Development Party (PPP) was scheduled to campaign in Jakarta on Tuesday but a party spokesman said it had cancelled electioneering because of weekend violence.
"We still have to see if the security forces can control the situation. I hope there will be no clash between the PPP and the security forces," an analyst with a local firm said.
"As you know sometimes the supporters are too excited (and are) beyond the control of the party," she added.
On Saturday and Sunday, PPP supporters clashed with police and loyalists of the ruling Golkar party in several parts of Jakarta.
Brokers also said that talk of lower-than-expected first quarter results of some blue chip counters such as Semen Gresik and Sampoerna could weaken sentiment.
"But there is always an opportunity to buy when the price has touched low levels. So investors might buy it up," an analyst with a Singapore-based firm said.
Local-led buying could continue in second and thirdliners such as shoe-maker Kasogi International, garment firm Ever Shine and confectionery firm Mayora Indah, brokers said.

Kasogi has been actively traded since last Friday due to a rights issue plan and a possible link-up with a foreign firm, brokers said. Evershine was likely to attract buyers on reports that it expects a 20 percent increase in its 1997 net profit.
On Monday, the Jakarta composite index fell 4.52 points to close at 652.55 points.
